entry.title: 🌐 Proxy vs Reverse Proxy – Explained Simply with Alice 🧠
entry.summary: When you hear the terms Proxy and Reverse Proxy, it might sound like network jargon. But don't worry—let’s break it down in plain English, and better yet, let's bring in Alice to help us understand it like a story. A Proxy (Forward Proxy) is like a middleman between you (the client) and the internet. When you use a proxy, you're not directly talking to the website—you send the request to the proxy, and it fetches the site for you. Key Point: It hides the client (you) from the internet. A Reverse Proxy is the opposite. It sits in front of servers and handles incoming requests. It decides which server should process the request and then responds back to the client.
